# Contract Comparison Report — No Documents Provided

Status: No contract texts were supplied. I cannot perform a line-by-line or section-by-section comparison without the source documents or summaries.

What I attempted to do
- I checked the input field `doc-summaries` and found it empty.
- Because there is no content to analyze, I did not fabricate or assume any contractual language or differences.

How you can proceed (what to provide)
1. Provide the two (or more) full contract texts, or
2. Provide clearly-labeled extracts (e.g., "Document A — Section 2.1: Term and Termination") for each document, or
3. Provide structured summaries keyed by section (JSON or plain text), with labels indicating which document each summary belongs to.

Minimum useful inputs
- Document A and Document B (preferably as plain text or PDF text extractions).
- Or, at minimum, the following sections for both documents:
  - Parties and definitions
  - Scope of work / Services / Deliverables
  - Term and termination (including notice requirements)
  - Payment, fees, invoicing, and expenses
  - Intellectual property ownership and licenses
  - Confidentiality and data protection
  - Limitation of liability and caps
  - Indemnities
  - Warranties and representations
  - Assignment and subcontracting
  - Governing law and dispute resolution
  - Amendment process and signatures

Recommended format for best results
- Prefer plain text or structured JSON where each section is labeled.
- If uploading PDFs, provide an extracted text copy (OCR if scanned).
- If the contracts have different section numbering, include headings so I can align by heading rather than number.

What I will produce once you supply documents
- A full markdown comparison report highlighting key differences and risks.
- A per-section diff array with:
  - section-name
  - document-a-text
  - document-b-text
  - difference-summary
  - significance (major/minor/identical)
- A short list of high-level key differences with impacts and recommended actions.
- An executive summary with the most important items to negotiate or review.

Guidance on significance classification (how I’ll decide)
- Major: Material differences that affect obligations, risk allocation, liability, payment, IP, termination rights, or compliance.
- Minor: Editorial differences, clarifications, thresholds, or timing issues that do not fundamentally reallocate risk.
- Identical: Substantially the same language or meaning.

Next step
- Paste the two contract texts or upload the section summaries and I will run a detailed comparison.

Prepared to proceed as soon as you provide the documents.
result.summary: No contracts were provided to compare. Please supply the full texts or labeled section summaries for Document A and Document B (see the "How you can proceed" section above). Once I have the documents, I will produce a detailed markdown report, per-section diffs with significance (major/minor/identical), a list of key differences with impact analysis, and an executive summary.
